active_paradigms.idea: Replace fixed-width beam search with admissible best-first branch-and-bound over transaction prefixes using heapq
active_paradigms.description: The current program evaluates true simulator costs for prefixes, which is a major strength, but then irrevocably discards all but at most eight prefixes and locally improves only four completed orders. Treat each prefix as a search-tree node and store it in a priority queue ordered by an admissible lower bound: at minimum, the simulator makespan of that prefix, since adding transactions cannot remove already required work. Obtain a feasible incumbent early from the current beam/greedy construction, then prune every prefix whose lower bound is already no better than that incumbent. Expand the most promising surviving prefix by appending each unplaced transaction, always scoring children through workload.get_opt_seq_cost rather than a surrogate. Add a conflict-aware secondary key, such as the remaining transaction's number of read/write conflicts with already placed transactions, only for tie-breaking; simulator cost remains the decision criterion. Use num_seqs as an expansion/evaluation budget so the search is anytime: it returns the incumbent if the budget expires, but can prove or approach optimality on smaller instances. Memoize full prefix costs and retain several distinct prefixes even when they have equal cost, because their future conflict orientations differ. This directly addresses the principal beam weakness while preserving what makes the existing solution effective: optimization against the exact evaluator-facing cost function.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: The sole evaluator-relevant quantity is the makespan returned by workload.get_opt_seq_cost for the final permutation. The priority and pruning bound should therefore be based on that exact makespan, not transaction length, write count, or a graph proxy.
active_paradigms.cautions: The visible evaluator wrapper only serializes calls and delegates to hidden evaluator.py, so do not assume any extra score component beyond the simulator result. The monotonic-prefix lower-bound argument must be verified against the simulator; if a partial prefix can report a cost larger than a later complete prefix, use the prefix value only as priority and disable cost-based pruning. Keep a hard evaluation/node budget, since factorial expansion is otherwise infeasible for large workloads.

active_paradigms.idea: Solve the operation-level disjunctive scheduling formulation directly as a mixed-integer linear program with scipy.optimize.milp
active_paradigms.description: Instead of searching permutations indirectly, formulate the schedule that the simulator is effectively evaluating. Create a start-time variable for every read/write operation and add unit-duration chain constraints for consecutive operations within each transaction. For every pair of operations from different transactions that conflict on a key, introduce a binary orientation variable deciding which operation precedes the other, with big-M precedence constraints in the chosen direction. Couple all conflict orientations between a transaction pair to a single binary transaction-order variable when the simulator requires one global order per transaction pair, and introduce integer rank variables plus standard rank/order constraints to eliminate cyclic transaction orders. Add a makespan variable constrained to be at least every operation completion time and minimize it with scipy.optimize.milp using integrality for orientation and rank variables. Convert the resulting transaction ranks into the required sequence, then call get_opt_seq_cost once to validate the candidate and return that exact cost rather than trusting the MILP objective. This differs fundamentally from the current beam-plus-local-search method: it considers all pairwise conflict directions jointly, so it can cross barriers requiring many simultaneous relocations or reversals. It is especially promising when transaction counts are modest but operations and repeated conflicts make local permutation neighborhoods deceptive.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Minimize the operation-level Cmax/makespan, with the final ordering selected by the exact workload.get_opt_seq_cost result. The MILP should model only read-write and write-write conflicts; read-read pairs must not introduce unnecessary serialization.
active_paradigms.cautions: This is correct only after matching the simulator semantics precisely, including operation durations, whether a conflict is enforced by transaction order or individual operation order, and any lock-release behavior. A naive per-operation orientation model may produce a schedule that cannot be represented by the single returned transaction permutation, so enforce global transaction-order consistency if required. Choose M from a safe upper bound such as the total number of operations, set a practical time_limit option, and fall back to the best incumbent sequence if scipy reports no feasible integer solution.

active_paradigms.idea: Use randomized large-neighborhood destroy-and-greedy-repair restarts driven entirely by exact simulator insertion costs
active_paradigms.description: The current descent examines relocations, swaps, and interval reversals only around a small set of deterministic beam finalists, so it cannot leave a basin when every one-transaction move is temporarily harmful. Start from the best current permutation, randomly remove a block of several transactions, and rebuild the partial order by inserting each removed transaction at every possible position while selecting the insertion with minimum workload.get_opt_seq_cost. Bias removal toward transactions participating in many actual read-write/write-write conflicts with the rest of the order, because changing those positions has the greatest chance to alter the critical path. Perform many independent destroy-and-repair attempts, retaining the globally best schedule, and vary removal size from small perturbations to a substantial fraction of transactions. For each repair, randomize the order in which removed transactions are reinserted; this explores different conflict orientations even when their initial insertion scores tie. Optionally accept a non-improving repaired schedule only as the seed for a later restart, while never replacing the globally reported best result. Every accept/reject comparison and every insertion choice uses the simulator cost, avoiding the unsupported length/write-count heuristics warned against in the task. This gives a much larger effective neighborhood than the current pair swaps and reversals without requiring a full factorial search.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Optimize final simulator makespan across diversified restarts; the conflict count is only used to choose which transactions to perturb, never as a substitute objective.
active_paradigms.cautions: Fix a local random.Random seed or derive it deterministically from workload contents if evaluator reproducibility matters; hidden scoring may penalize unstable outcomes. Bound the number of candidate insertion evaluations and restarts by num_seqs or a fixed budget, since repair cost grows with removal size and transaction count. Always preserve a valid complete permutation and return workload.get_opt_seq_cost(best_sequence), not a stale cached or surrogate value.

tried_paradigms.idea: Use exact permutation enumeration for small transaction counts with itertools.permutations
tried_paradigms.description: The current program is a deterministic beam search over prefixes, followed by relocation, swap, and interval-reversal descent. Its key strength is that every comparison uses workload.get_opt_seq_cost rather than a surrogate based only on lengths or write counts. However, its beam discards prefixes solely on partial-prefix cost, even though a prefix that is temporarily expensive can produce a substantially better final dependency orientation; its local neighborhoods also cannot cross deep permutation valleys. When n is small enough that n! simulator calls fit the evaluation budget, replace heuristic construction entirely with itertools.permutations(range(n)) and score every complete permutation using get_opt_seq_cost. Retain the minimum cost and use lexicographic order as a deterministic tie-breaker. This directly optimizes exactly the same scalar the simulator and evaluator use, so it is globally optimal rather than merely locally optimal. A practical guarded implementation can enumerate exactly only below a conservative cutoff and use the incumbent beam method above that cutoff, but the exact branch should be preferred whenever workloads have roughly 8–9 transactions or fewer. This is fundamentally different from trying to tune the current beam width or add another local move.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: The actual makespan returned by workload.get_opt_seq_cost; exact enumeration removes all prefix-ranking and local-optimum errors for feasible workload sizes.
tried_paradigms.cautions: Do not evaluate partial permutations as though they were comparable to final schedules in the exact path. Cache complete tuple costs only if repeated evaluations can arise, and choose the factorial cutoff from the evaluator timeout and observed get_opt_seq_cost latency. Preserve the required return shape of (best_cost, best_sequence).

tried_paradigms.idea: Use simulator-guided randomized iterated local search with random.Random.shuffle perturbations
tried_paradigms.description: The existing search is deterministic: all beam branches are ranked by the same partial-cost rule, and only the best few complete finalists receive improvement. Consequently it can repeatedly converge to the same basin, particularly when many initial single-transaction costs tie. Use a dedicated seeded random.Random instance to generate diverse full permutation starts and, after a local optimum is reached, perturb it by shuffling a selected block or a selected set of transaction positions before applying the same simulator-scored relocation and exchange descent. Accept strictly improving global incumbents, but also continue from perturbed local optima rather than restarting only from greedy prefixes. This targets the principal blind spot of the present code: a beneficial schedule may require several individually non-improving order changes before its conflict directions become favorable. Allocate the number of perturbation/restart attempts from num_seqs, so the caller’s search-budget parameter controls diversity rather than merely limiting beam width. Score every candidate with get_opt_seq_cost, never with operation counts or conflict counts, because the simulator captures timing and overlap effects that a static heuristic misses. A fixed seed makes the result reproducible for an evaluator while still exploring basins that the current deterministic beam cannot reach.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Lower makespan through escape from relocation/swap/reversal local minima and broader coverage of full-order permutation space.
tried_paradigms.cautions: Use a local Random instance with a fixed deterministic seed; do not use unseeded global randomness, which can add evaluator variance. Bound the number of full simulator calls carefully, retain the globally best schedule even when exploring worse perturbed states, and avoid perturbing only adjacent items because that is too similar to the current swap neighborhood.

tried_paradigms.idea: Generate a conflict-structure spectral order using numpy.linalg.eigh
tried_paradigms.description: Build an undirected weighted transaction-conflict matrix directly from the workload operations: for each pair of transactions and each common key, add weight only when at least one access is a write, with weight proportional to the number of conflicting access pairs. Form its graph Laplacian and call numpy.linalg.eigh on that symmetric matrix. Sort transaction indices by the Fiedler-vector coordinate to obtain a global spectral ordering candidate, and evaluate that complete order with get_opt_seq_cost. Unlike the current beam, this considers all transactions and their conflict topology simultaneously before committing to early prefix choices. The rationale is that transactions with strongly coupled conflict patterns are positioned coherently, avoiding arbitrary early orientations caused by ties in one-transaction prefix cost; disconnected components can be deterministically concatenated because they have no cross-conflict contribution. Evaluate both the Fiedler order and its reverse, because an undirected Laplacian has no preferred direction whereas read/write sequence direction changes the simulator’s makespan. This is a cheap, structurally distinct seed that can outperform greedy prefix selection on dense clustered conflict graphs, and it can also be compared directly against the current beam result using the exact simulator objective.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Makespan lost by myopic prefix construction, especially on workloads whose conflict graph has clusters or near-disconnected components that should be ordered as coherent groups.
tried_paradigms.cautions: Extract operation/key information using the actual Workload representation rather than assuming a nonexistent public field; if only the input mapping is accessible, parse it consistently with Workload. Read-read overlaps must have zero edge weight. Handle all-zero or disconnected Laplacians deterministically, and do not assume the spectral score itself predicts makespan: get_opt_seq_cost must select the final winner.
